claims.text: The base alloy has composition Cr16Mn16Fe16Co16Ni16P20 in atomic percent.
The base alloy solidifies into several primary non-eutectic crystalline phases.
The base alloy exhibits a complex, multistep crystallization sequence.
Approximately 2 at% boron should be added by partially replacing phosphorus.
A roughly 2 at% boron addition will suppress heterogeneous nucleation during cooling.
Boron will modify local atomic arrangements in the alloy.
Boron will increase the liquid viscosity.
The boron-induced structural and viscosity changes will perturb long-range ordering and formation of primary crystalline nuclei.
Boron atoms disrupt the structural ordering required to form stable primary non-eutectic phases.
Suppression of primary-phase nucleation will extend the supercooled-liquid region.
Suppression of primary-phase nucleation will promote glass formation and increase amorphous retention.
The boron-modified alloy will retain a higher amorphous fraction than the unmodified alloy.
The boron-modified alloy will exhibit delayed crystallization exotherms during reheating.
The boron-modified alloy will exhibit less intense crystallization exotherms during reheating.
The boron addition will increase the alloy's thermal stability.
The predicted improvement is expected at cooling rates above approximately 10^2 K/s.
There is a possibility that the boron addition will form unwanted boride phases.

contradictions.description: Delayed crystallization onset and reduced exotherm intensity are predicted as supporting outcomes, but the falsification rule states that the hypothesis is falsified when the modified samples both exhibit an elevated onset temperature and reduced exotherm intensity, alongside no amorphous-fraction increase. Thus, two predicted successes are incorrectly included as falsifying conditions.
